 CORAM:HONOURABLE MR. JUSTICE NIKHIL S. KARIEL
Date : 05/01/2026  ORAL ORDER 1.
Heard learned Advocate Mr. Kuldeep Vaidya on behalf of the applicant and learned Additional Public Prosecutor Mr. L.B. Dabhi on behalf of respondent- State.
2. Rule.
Learned APP and learned Advocate waive service of rule on behalf of the respective respondents.

3. The present applicant who has been arraigned as an accused has preferred this application under Section 483 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 for enlarging the applicant on Regular Bail in connection with FIR being FIR No. 11191011220164 of 2022 registered with D.C.B. Police Station, Ahmedabad City for the offences punishable under Sections 409, 420, 465, 467, 471, 120B,
34 of the Indian Penal Code after filing of the charge-sheet.

sentences.text: Learned Advocate on behalf of the applicant would submit that considering the role attributed to the applicant, and nature of the allegation levelled against, the applicant may be enlarged on regular bail.

It is further NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/27634/2025 ORDER DATED: 05/01/2026 undefined submitted that since the charge-sheet is filed no useful purpose would be served by keeping the applicant in jail for indefinite period.
It is further submitted that applicant is ready and willing to abide by all the conditions that may be imposed by this Court if released on bail.

5. The present application is vehemently objected to by learned APP on behalf of respondent- State by submitting that looking to the nature of offence and the role attributed to the present applicant,
this Court may not exercise the discretion in favour of the applicant and the application may be dismissed.

6. This Court has heard learned Advocates for the respective parties and perused the FIR including charge-sheet as well as order passed by learned Session Court as well as affidavit filed by the investigating officer before the learned Trial Court.

7. This Court has taken into consideration the law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Sanjay Chandra v. Central Bureau of Investigation reported in [2012] 1 SCC 40.
8.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
This Court has also considered the following aspects:
(i) While the allegation in the FIR being that the accused had created fictitious firms based upon forged documents and had created fake transactions worth Crores of Rupees and had availed benefit of input tax credit using the said documents and the State had been defrauded to the tune of more than Rs. 600 Crores, and whereas the role attributed to the present applicant appearing to be very limited, in inasmuch as the applicant had NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/27634/2025 ORDER DATED:
05/01/2026 undefined purchased bogus bills of Rs. 20-22 lacs from the main accused.
(ii) The fact of the main accused and all the arrested accused having been considered for being enlarged on regular bail by this Court.
(iii) The fact of the present applicant being in custody since 09.09.2025 and the charge-sheet having been laid.

9. In the facts and circumstances of the case and considering the nature of the allegations made against in the First Information Report, without discussing the evidence in detail, prima facie, this Court is of the opinion that this is a fit case to exercise the discretion and enlarge the applicant on regular bail.
10. Hence, the present application is allowed.

The applicant is ordered to be released on bail in connection with FIR being FIR No. 11191011220164 of 2022 registered with D.C.B. Police Station,
Madhav Pratapbhai Patel vs State Of Gujarat on 5 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/72307637/
2

Ahmedabad City on executing a bond of Rs. 50,000/- ( Rupees Fifty Thousand ) with one surety of the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court and subject to the conditions that he shall;
[a] not take undue advantage of liberty or misuse liberty;
The Authorities will release the applicant only if he is not required in connection with any other offence for the time being.
If breach of any of the above conditions is committed, the Sessions Judge concerned will be free to take appropriate action in the matter.
12. Bail bond to be executed before the lower court having jurisdiction to try the case.
It will be open for the concerned Court to delete, modify and/or relax any of the above conditions in accordance with law.

13. At the stage of trial, the trial court shall not be influenced by any observations of this Court which are of preliminary nature made at this stage, only for the purpose of considering the application of the applicant for being released on regular bail.
14. The application is allowed in the aforesaid terms.
Rule is made absolute to the aforesaid extent.
Direct service is permitted.

(NIKHIL S. KARIEL,J) NIRU Madhav Pratapbhai Patel vs State Of Gujarat on 5 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/72307637/
